data.title: QVC Group Issues Cautionary Bankruptcy Operating Reports
data.description:
The latest update is out from QVC Group, Inc. ( (QVCG) ).

On April 16, 2026, QVC Group, Inc. and affiliated entities filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas to implement a prepackaged reorganization plan. The court confirmed the plan on July 20, 2026, and the company parties emerged from Chapter 11 on August 6, 2026, marking the formal completion of the court-supervised restructuring process.

To comply with bankruptcy reporting requirements, the company parties filed monthly operating reports on September 11, 2026, covering financial data as of July 31, 2026 and activity for July. QVC cautioned that these unaudited reports, prepared solely for Bankruptcy Code compliance and differing from regular Exchange Act reporting, may be subject to future adjustments and should not be relied upon as indicative of its current or future consolidated financial condition or performance.

data.title: Rainmaker Worldwide Restructures Leadership and Board Governance
data.description:
Rainmaker Worldwide ( (RAKR) ) has provided an announcement.

Effective September 10, 2026, Rainmaker Worldwide Inc. and Larchwood Management Partners Inc. mutually terminated the Interim CEO Services Agreement under which Michael O’Connor had served as interim chief executive, with final service fees and expenses fixed and no early termination penalty. Interest will accrue on the unpaid balance of fees and expenses from September 11, 2026 until paid, after which the parties will grant limited mutual releases related to compensation under the terminated agreement.

On the same date, following the appointment of Ryan D. Moore and Michael A. Skinner to the board, O’Connor resigned as director, chairman, interim CEO and principal executive officer citing health concerns, and agreed to assist with an orderly transition of records and responsibilities. Before resigning, O’Connor expanded the board from one to three members and appointed Moore and Skinner, who had been recommended by holders of Series A preferred stock and now constitute the full board with one vacancy remaining.

data.title: Cosma S.A. Secures Exclusive Polish Rights With Medical Cannabis Acquisition
data.description:
Cosma S.A. ( (PL:COS) ) has provided an announcement.

Cosma S.A. has signed an investment agreement to acquire 100% of IMP_C sp. z o.o., a Warsaw-based company active in the medical marijuana sector whose key assets are regulatory approvals and applications for cannabis-based medicinal products. IMP_C, to be renamed FULL SPECTRUM sp. z o.o., holds a registered medical cannabis flower product and three cannabis oil products in registration, positioning Cosma to expand its cannabinoid portfolio.

The transaction is structured in two stages, with Cosma already acquiring 50% of IMP_C and assuming full operational control and financing responsibilities while due diligence is conducted. The second stage, to be completed by end-2027 at the latest, is contingent on regulatory clearance for lawful import and distribution of the products in Poland and repayment of existing liabilities by the sellers.

Although the purchase price is not material to Cosma’s scale, the agreement includes a performance-based consideration for the sellers tied to product sales over five years, without a monetary cap and payable quarterly. This aligns seller incentives with the commercialization success of Cannabis Flos and cannabis oils, potentially increasing variable costs for Cosma as sales volumes grow.

Following satisfaction of regulatory conditions, Cosma and Israel-based Bazelet Pharma Ltd. will enter a distribution agreement under which Bazelet will supply Cannabis Flos and cannabis oils at a fixed price, and Cosma will purchase exclusively from Bazelet for 24 months. Cosma will hold exclusive rights to sell and commercialize these products in Poland, reinforcing its market positioning in medical cannabis.

The company plans to import the products via its existing licensed wholesaler INTERFARMED CANNABIS, ensuring regulatory compliance and centralized control over import and distribution. Management views the deal as a strategic step in developing cannabinoid-based products, broadening the product range and integrating regulatory processes, which could strengthen Cosma’s footprint in the emerging Polish medical cannabis market.
